stops.name: El/Ella: Book of Magic Love
stops.campa: From the exile at Montagnola comes El/Ella: Libro del Amor Mágico, 'He/She: Book of Magic Love,' the book of the doctrine born at Irene's grave. In it He and She are the two poles of the one divine being, sundered and seeking reunion through the tantric way, through A-Mor without-death. The dead Beloved is raised into the eternal feminine, the guide up the mountain. Of all his books it is the one his readers hold nearest the heart of the myth: the love-mysticism that underlies even the war-cosmology, the tears that opened at Montségur set down as scripture.

stops.name: Santiago, El Cordón Dorado, the Golden Thread
stops.campa: He publishes El Cordón Dorado, the Golden Thread, the first panel of the great mythological cycle he now unfolds, in which he narrates a hidden cosmos of Hyperborea and the Black Sun, of the vanquished withdrawn beyond the poles, of an initiatory order stretching from Atlantis to the Andes. It is the myth he has authored across a lifetime, the strung thread that joins Melimoyu to Kailash to the Antarctic door to the burnt pog of the Cathars. Whatever the world makes of its dark matter, it is his own cosmos, built stone by stone from the ice up.

stops.name: Santiago, the return to Chile at Santa Lucía
stops.campa: In 1980 the wanderer comes home, to an apartment in the Barrio Bellas Artes beneath the green hill of Santa Lucía in the heart of Santiago, again at the foot of the cordillera where his life began. From here he writes NOS: Book of the Resurrection, the book of the return of the vanquished and of the dead Beloved, of the polar door reopening. The old poet keeps a kind of court; disciples climb to his rooms. His life has bent back upon its origin: the orphan of the Andes, grown old, dwells once more in the shadow of the sacred mountain.

stops.name: Santiago: Adolf Hitler, el Último Avatãra
stops.campa: He publishes the central panel of his war-cycle, Adolf Hitler, el Último Avatãra: in his mythology the tenth and last avatar of the Hindu reckoning, the incarnation that closes an age, a figure of Wotan risen at the end of the Kali Yuga. It is the darkest chamber of the cosmos he has authored, the myth by which he reads the whole catastrophe of the century as sacred defeat and coming return. Set down here as the mythos he made, not as any truth of the world, it is the pole of his esoteric Hitlerism: the vanquished as the awaited, withdrawn beyond the ice, to come again.

stops.name: Santiago, Memorias de Él y Yo, the alchemy of a life
stops.campa: In his old age Serrano sets down his life in four great volumes, the Memorias de Él y Yo, 'Memoirs of He and I,' reckoned among the finest autobiographies in the Chilean tongue. He orders the story by the colours of alchemy: the black of the nigredo, the white of the albedo, the red of the rubedo, the gold of the return. The orphaning, the mountains, the ice, the Beloved, Jung and Hesse, Kailash and Montségur, all are gathered as stations of a single Work, a life read as the transmutation of lead into the gold of the interior Mountain.

stops.name: Santiago, death at the foot of the cordillera
stops.campa: On the twenty-eighth of February, in his apartment beneath Santa Lucía, a stroke takes Miguel Serrano at ninety-one, at the foot of the same Andes over which he was born. He dies as he lived, certain that an Avatar can never truly die, that the parted lovers are reunited beyond the poles, that the golden thread runs on unbroken. The poet of the mountain lays down the pen after nine decades of building his myth. Outside the window the cordillera stands white and enormous, the eastern wall of the world, unchanged since it first looked down on the newborn on Calle Santo Domingo.
stops.quote_source: Miguel Serrano, recalled by his son José Serrano Rosselot

stops.name: Cementerio General de Santiago, the last road, past the martyrs
stops.campa: He is carried into the Cementerio General, more than a hundred following: kin, writers, disciples of the myth. The cortège takes a deliberate road, and the coffin halts before the memorial of the Seguro Obrero, the fallen youths of 1938 whose massacre had turned him seventy years before. The circle closes at the graveside where it opened: the martyrs of his young manhood receive the old mythographer at the end. He is laid down in the earth of Santiago, beneath the cordillera, the golden thread, in his own faith, passing on beyond the poles.
